title: Intel Foundry lands a second external AI-chip customer on 18A by Q2 2027
body: The semiconductor tape's June 8 snap-back - Intel up about 8.5% and Micron about 9% reversing the prior Friday's roughly $1 trillion Broadcom-driven washout - was led not by GPU-demand names but by two US-manufacturing catalysts: reporting that Alphabet had tapped Intel to manufacture about 3 million in-house chips, and that Nvidia was evaluating Intel's 18A process for future parts. The signal that matters is not the one-day price move but who carried it - the market rotated leadership from the merchant-GPU vendors that led the prior run toward domestic foundry capacity, repricing Intel specifically as a contract manufacturer for other companies' custom AI silicon rather than only as a struggling CPU vendor. A single hyperscaler engagement plus one fabless evaluation does not yet establish Intel Foundry as a credible second-source merchant fab for leading-edge AI parts; it could remain a one-off in-house Alphabet job and an evaluation that never converts. The forward thesis is that the Alphabet 18A signal hardens into an external-customer franchise: by Q2 2027 at least one additional named hyperscaler or fabless AI-chip designer beyond the initial Alphabet engagement publicly commits to manufacturing a leading-edge AI accelerator, custom inference ASIC, or networking part on an Intel Foundry advanced node (18A or its 14A successor) - confirmed via an on-record customer announcement, a signed foundry agreement, a tape-out disclosure, or an executive statement naming the part - with Nvidia's reported 18A evaluation the leading candidate to convert. The marker is a committed external leading-edge customer for a named AI part, not a packaging-only deal, a memorandum of intent, or further unconfirmed evaluation reporting. The counter-risk is that 18A yield or schedule slips and the prospective customers stay with TSMC for leading-edge AI volume, leaving Intel's external book limited to the in-house Alphabet work and trailing-edge fill.

reasoning.because: June 8: Alphabet tapped Intel to make ~3M in-house chips; Nvidia evaluating Intel 18A; INTC +8.5%
reasoning.given: the chip rebound rotated leadership to domestic foundry capacity, repricing Intel as a merchant fab
reasoning.so_that: a second named hyperscaler or fabless designer commits a leading-edge AI part to an Intel Foundry node
reasoning.landing: by Q2 2027; >=1 external Intel-Foundry 18A/14A AI-chip customer beyond Alphabet
reasoning.plain_language: After Alphabet hired Intel to build its chips and Nvidia started testing Intel's factory, another big chip buyer will likely sign on too.

summary: Intel's June 8 rebound ran on US-manufacturing catalysts - Alphabet tapping Intel to make ~3M in-house chips and Nvidia evaluating its 18A process - repricing Intel as a merchant fab for custom AI silicon. Expect Intel Foundry to win a second named external leading-edge AI-chip customer by Q2 2027.
